To date, the MNRTF has awarded more than $1.3 billion in grants throughout Michigan’s 83 counties. This includes 35 projects in Bay County, contrasted with 110 funded projects in Ottawa County and 106 in Kent County.

It is for these reasons that Bay Area Community Foundation, Heart of the Lakes, The Conservation Fund-Great Lakes Office, Saginaw County Parks and Recreation, and Spicer Engineering came together to host the MNRTF Board of Directors and staff from Michigan Department of Natural Resources for a bus-and-walking tour of local project sites in October 2022.

Diane Mahoney, BACF President and CEO, greeted representatives who came from all over Michigan at the Bay City State Park. Before the tour began, she highlighted the connection between community amenities and economic development. “Community development is economic development. It has never been more apparent than it is nowadays when people are choosing where to live and not where to work,” Mahoney said.

U.S. Rep. Dan Kildee, D-Flint Township, praised the work of the program represented at the meeting. He said some of his defining memories are from time spent outdoors in Michigan. “I grew up in Flint, but I spent a lot of time on Lake Huron,” he said. Kildee talked about the importance of investing in older, chronically-distressed communities to enhance their capacity. He said he’s in favor of incentives to encourage these types of investments. However, he said he’s also cautious about development that sacrifices natural spaces. Instead, he said it’s important to preserve the natural beauty of the state and encourage green spaces.

Jonathan Jarosz, executive director of Heart of the Lakes, which is a statewide organization of land conservations in Michigan, said the day’s theme was exploring partnerships between local organizations and the Trust Fund that have improved access along the Saginaw River. One of the highlighted areas was the Bay City State Park, which opened in 1923. Dan Eichinger, then-director of Michigan's Department of Natural Resources, talked about driving past Bay City State Park as a child with his father and grandfather on Sunday afternoons.
